Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick tour last week. As part of our vendor intake we need a short attestation of your RTO/RPO commitments for the core text-generation API plus a single-sheet recovery matrix that shows restoration steps for the following scenarios: regional outage, single-cluster failure, and cold-start recovery after a complete cache wipe.

In addition, our security team asked for a SIG mapping that calls out any gaps between Redwood's BCP controls and the SIG control set (especially items in continuity & availability domain). A high-level PDF that lists gaps + mitigations would be fine.

Can you provide those artifacts by end of week? If there are any controls that require legal covenants (data residency or runbook access), flag them and we'll loop Legal Ops.

Appreciate it,
Samantha

Adding a couple operational notes inline — copying the working draft in case it's helpful.

On 21 Sep 2026 11:03, Priyom Das wrote:
> Two quick clarifying points before we finalize: 
> 1) For 'core text-generation API' do you want per-model RTO/RPO (some models run on pre-warmed pools vs. on-demand cold starts) or a single conservative commitment across the product?

We recommend providing per-class commitments:
- Pre-warmed (reserved/dedicated) pools: target RTO 2 minutes, RPO near-zero (KV cache warm).
- On-demand (cold-start quantized models): target RTO 20-30 minutes depending on model size and region; RPO depends on caching and request routing and should be documented as worst-case for customer-owned session state.

> 2) For recovery evidence, would a sample of runbook snippets + test logs (redacted) suffice, or do you need full runbook access?

Sample snippets + signed attestation + one recent test log should be acceptable for most vendors. If Starlite requires live runbook access (zoom walk-through or read-only drive access), we can coordinate that as an escalated request.

I'll validate the RTO/RPO numbers in the attached matrix and add a short note about test cadence.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Reliability & Observability | Redwood Inference
